perspective:
Sara Manuelito’s available information:

- Sara is an American Indian Speech-Language Pathologist at a community health center. She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a nurse, long-time colleague, and close friend.
- Sara attends the funeral of a mutual patient with Shirley. She observes Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspects Shirley is deeply affected by the loss.
- Sara tells Shirley she knows this is hard, that she saw how much Shirley cared for the patient, that they did everything they could, and that they should remember the good care and moments of joy they provided.
- Sara hears Shirley say it has been tough, that she keeps thinking something more could have been done, and that it is hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara brings up their treatment decisions because she senses Shirley feels burdened. Shirley tells Sara she feels responsible and wonders if pushing for a different approach might have helped.
- Sara tells Shirley they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden is too heavy to carry alone. Shirley says she appreciates this but finds it hard to accept.
- Sara observes Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet office moment, Sara confronts her, saying she noticed Shirley holding back feelings and that it is okay to be open.
- Shirley tells Sara she is not sure she can be open and does not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara replies that showing emotion does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley says maybe Sara is right and she will try to be more open.
- Sara later thinks her previous confrontation may have been too harsh. She apologizes to Shirley for coming on too strong.
- Shirley tells Sara it was a bit much but that she knows Sara meant well and appreciates the apology. Sara says she is there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanks her and says they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara notices Shirley’s demeanor has improved and feels hopeful. She asks how Shirley is feeling.
- Shirley says she is feeling better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggests spending more time together outside work. Shirley agrees, and they plan something for the weekend.
